title: Introduction to neuroscience: brain and behavior
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Survey the nervous system from cells to behavior: neurons and glia, electrical and chemical signaling in outline, the organization of the brain, how sensory systems and movement work, learning and memory, emotion and motivation, sleep, language and thought, development and plasticity, disorders of the brain, and the methods neuroscientists use, with the history of the main discoveries.
primary_reading: Neuroscience Online, an open-access textbook from McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston (free)

weeks.1: Neurons, glia and the neuron doctrine
weeks.2: Electrical signals: resting and action potentials in outline
weeks.4: The organization of the nervous system
weeks.5: Sensory systems: from receptors to perception
weeks.6: Movement: muscles, motor cortex, basal ganglia and cerebellum
weeks.9: Sleep, rhythms and consciousness in outline
weeks.10: Language, thought and the cerebral cortex
weeks.12: Disorders of the brain and the methods of neuroscience

blocks.deliverable: Label the parts of a neuron and trace a signal through it.
Map the major brain regions and their main functions.
Trace one sensation and one movement through the nervous system.
Week 7 midterm; explain a classic memory case and what it showed.
Summarize the evidence for one localized function and its limits.
Compare what three research methods can and cannot show.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Brain systems guide: write an illustrated-in-words guide to one brain system (for example vision, memory or reward) that traces it from molecules and cells to behavior, explains one classic experiment and one clinical case, and lists three open questions, with a one-page quiz and answer key for a classmate.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
